memories.content: Link each HCI research question directly to corresponding user data and analysis procedures.
In preregistered studies, specify the conditions under which deviations from the plan are permissible.
In preregistered studies, specify how to record content that deviates from the plan.
Commit to one exact target number of participants so the schedule, workload, and budget can be checked against the same quantity.
Specify the interview protocols, recording devices, or log tools used to collect each type of user data.
Specify whether each type of user data is collected before, during, or after the interaction.
Readers cannot tell whether the schedule and budget agree when different sections imply different target counts.
In formative evaluation prototypes, implementation instability exists as an independent cause of task failure alongside design choices.
If a prototype safety signal occurs during formative evaluation, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over planned data collection.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to the data and analysis.
The author of this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Calculate the required sessions, facilitator hours, and participant payments from the same exact target rather than from separate rough estimates.
If recruitment falls below the exact target, state the shortfall explicitly and revise the affected schedule or deliverable.
Do not use a wide range merely to postpone choosing the quantity that the rest of the proposal must support.
Conduct one review prior to submission focusing solely on the validity of user problems, system interventions, and field evaluation logic.
Cross-check whether research questions align with the core functions of the system.
Cross-check whether field tasks align with representative measures.
Cross-check whether the evidence to be collected aligns with the design and operational decisions to be changed.
Finally verify that the user problem, system intervention, field evaluation, and expected contribution form one coherent logical flow.
HCI reviewers view the validity of design interventions as low if research questions do not connect to system functions.
HCI reviewers view the validity of evaluation plans as low if field tasks fail to generate representative measures.
HCI reviewers view the practical utility of contributions as low if collected evidence cannot change design or operational decisions.
Before submission, conduct a sequential walkthrough with field liaisons of installation failures, operational interruptions, and recovery scenarios.
Verify in one sentence how each proposed contribution could actually alter specific design or operational decisions.
The user must distinguish unconfirmed field partners and equipment from finalized ones so remaining execution risks can be assessed.

analysis.overview: Both frames emphasize proposal traceability and useful contribution claims. They complement each other on research-question alignment and decision-relevant evidence, while assigning different technical-failure practices to formative evaluation and pre-submission planning. Each also contains distinct methodological, safety, resourcing, review, and execution-risk guidance.

relations.reason: The reference requires question-to-data-and-analysis paths, while the compared frame requires question-to-system-function alignment and identifies its review consequence; these complementary checks govern research-question validity.
relations.summary: Research questions should be traceable to the system functions and evidentiary analysis needed to establish an answerable, valid design rationale.

relations.reason: The reference identifies feature-list presentation as a contribution-claim weakness, while the compared frame requires collected evidence and proposed contributions to show decision-changing utility.
relations.summary: Contribution claims should demonstrate practical relevance to specific design or operational decisions rather than rely on implemented features alone.

relations.reason: The explicit stages explain the different practices: implementation instability is an independent cause of formative task failure, whereas installation failures, interruptions, and recovery are walked through prospectively with field liaisons.
relations.summary: Technical failures require evaluation-stage attribution during formative studies and scenario-based operational review before submission.

relations.reason: These reference-side statements are complementary parts of one deviation-governance policy not supplied by the compared frame.
relations.summary: Preregistered studies should define when deviations are permissible and how deviating content is recorded.

relations.reason: These reference-side statements jointly establish and justify one exact-target planning policy, including consequences of inconsistent estimates or recruitment shortfalls.
relations.summary: A proposal should use one exact participant target across schedule, workload, budget, payments, recruitment reporting, and deliverable revision.

relations.reason: These reference-side statements split the procedural and temporal components of one data-collection specification absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Each user-data type should identify its collection method or tool and its timing relative to interaction.

relations.reason: This conditional safety-priority rule appears only in the reference frame and is independently useful.
relations.summary: During formative evaluation, institutional safety procedures supersede planned data collection when a prototype safety signal occurs.

relations.reason: The compared-side statements describe complementary parts of one holistic validity and coherence review not supplied by the reference frame.
relations.summary: Before submission, the proposal should receive a focused review of the coherent logic linking user problems, interventions, field evaluation, and expected contributions.

relations.reason: The compared-side statements express the same task-to-measure validation claim as an instruction and its reviewer-facing rationale.
relations.summary: Field tasks should be checked for alignment with representative measures because misalignment weakens evaluation-plan validity.

relations.reason: This compared-side disclosure requirement is independently useful and has no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Unconfirmed field partners and equipment should be distinguished from finalized commitments so execution risks remain assessable.

reports.both: Both connect research questions to defensible system or evidence pathways and assess contributions by their ability to influence design or operational decisions.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame adds holistic logic review, task-to-measure validation, and disclosure of unconfirmed partners and equipment.
reports.differences: Technical failures are treated as attribution factors during formative evaluation but as scenarios for pre-submission walkthroughs with field liaisons.
reports.reference_only: The reference adds preregistration deviation rules, exact participant-target planning, data-collection specifications, and safety-procedure precedence.
